APT29.narrative: In December 2020, CISA released Alert AA20-352A regarding an Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) actor attributed as APT29 / Nobelium / Cozy Bear conducting a global supply chain compromise via SolarWinds Orion. The threat actor inserted a malicious backdoor known as SUNBURST (Solorigate) into Orion platform software builds. Upon execution, SUNBURST stayed dormant for up to two weeks before resolving primary command-and-control (C2) domains including avsvmcloud[.]com, using dynamically constructed DGA subdomains to exfiltrate host reconnaissance. Secondary stagers including TEARDROP and Raindrop memory-only droppers communicated with C2 IP 185.225.17.42 and backup infrastructure freescanonline[.]com (hosted at 20.140.8.11). APT29 systematically exploited Exchange vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-26855 ProxyLogon) for lateral movement and forged SAML tokens to compromise cloud identities (MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise and T1078 Valid Accounts).

Sandworm Team.origin: Russian Main Intelligence Directorate (GRU Main Center for Special Technologies)
Sandworm Team.narrative: CISA Advisory AA22-054A exposes destructive cyber attacks executed by Sandworm Team against industrial control systems (ICS). Sandworm engineered Industroyer (CrashOverride) and Industroyer2 to transmit IEC 60870-5-104 commands directly opening electrical transmission circuit breakers. Auxiliary wipers including NotPetya and CaddyWiper were staged via domains kiev-energy-update[.]com and grid-telemetry-sync[.]org on IPs 194.28.172.10 and 91.242.217.5. Initial penetration leverages EternalBlue SMB vulnerability CVE-2017-0144 and Fortinet VPN exploits, culminating in automated data destruction (MITRE ATT&CK T1485 Data Destruction and T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application).

Lazarus Group.narrative: Joint Cybersecurity Advisory CISA AA22-110A documents North Korean state-sponsored cyber operations targeting cryptocurrency and blockchain firms. Lazarus Group distributes the AppleJeus malware suite hidden inside trojanized trading applications distributed via domain secure-crypto-wallet[.]org and trading-desk-pro[.]com. C2 infrastructure is hosted on IP 175.45.176.8 (Ryugyong-dong Pyongyang allocation) and compromised intermediary VPSs. Lazarus operators exploit Apache Log4j CVE-2021-44228 to gain initial access to server clusters, deploying BLINDINGCAN and AppleJeus implants utilizing multi-stage payload obfuscation (MITRE ATT&CK T1566.002 Spearphishing Link and T1027 Obfuscated Files or Information) to facilitate illicit digital asset theft.

APT28.narrative: Advisory CISA AA23-074A details persistent cyber operations by Russian military intelligence GRU Unit 26165 (APT28). APT28 actively weaponizes Microsoft Outlook zero-day CVE-2023-23397 (elevation of privilege via Net-NTLMv2 hash relay). Spearphishing payloads deploy the Zebrocy modular malware family and Golang downloaders, communicating via domain auth-microsoft365[.]com and staging server mail-update-service[.]net hosted on IP 185.141.63.12. APT28 leverages credential access via NTLM stealing (MITRE ATT&CK T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment and T1059.001 PowerShell command execution) to target governmental, diplomatic, and defense entities across NATO members.

Volt Typhoon.origin: People's Republic of China State-Sponsored Actor
Volt Typhoon.narrative: Joint Advisory CISA AA24-038A details PRC state-sponsored group Volt Typhoon compromising critical infrastructure sectors across the United States (communications, energy, transportation, water). Volt Typhoon emphasizes living-off-the-land (LotL) techniques, abusing built-in Windows admin binaries (wmic, netsh, ntdsutil) rather than traditional malware. To build resilient proxy networks, the group deploys the KV-botnet and Fast Reverse Proxy (FRP) across end-of-life SOHO routers routing through 198.51.100.44 and 203.0.113.88 with dynamic domains like cisco-gateway-mesh[.]org. The actor exploits FortiOS SSL-VPN vulnerability CVE-2023-27997 for edge appliance infiltration and maintains years-long persistence via stolen administrator credentials (MITRE ATT&CK T1078 Valid Accounts and T1572 Protocol Tunneling).

FIN7.origin: Eastern European Financially Motivated Cybercrime Syndicate
FIN7.narrative: Mandiant threat analysis and DOJ indictments identify FIN7 as a prolific financially motivated syndicate operating under front companies like Combi Security. FIN7 conducts highly targeted spearphishing against hospitality, restaurant, and retail sectors to steal millions of payment card records. Initial lures deliver weaponized Word docs dropping GRIFFON lightweight JScript backdoors communicating with doc-secure-share[.]info on IP 193.106.191.4. FIN7 actively weaponizes ZeroLogon CVE-2020-1472 against Active Directory Domain Controllers to achieve domain dominance, subsequently staging Carbanak malware to siphon Point-of-Sale (POS) transactions (MITRE ATT&CK T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment and T1059.003 Windows Command Shell).
